content.text: continue the investigation of issue #37 and report the exact reason
I’ll pick up the repo investigation by checking Entire’s current guidance, then inspect issue #37 and the code paths it touches for a reproducible, evidence-backed cause.

The repository points to a concrete symptom: a thin DWM frame around the opaque black/white panel, with two attempted fixes and a revert in history. I’m checking the issue report and those commits now to distinguish the visual symptom from its underlying Windows composition cause.

**Issue #37’s original border has a specific cause:** opaque panels set `DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR` to `DWMWA_COLOR_DEFAULT`. DWM interprets that as “draw the system border,” which puts a 1-DIP frame over the panel’s outer pixels. The issue measured it as 1 px at 100–150% scaling and 2 px at 200%. The CSS border is commented out. [Issue #37](https://github.com/haxllo/nex/issues/37) · [Microsoft’s DWM attribute docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dwmapi/ne-dwmapi-dwmwindowattribute)

The square corners have a separate cause: opaque black/white WebView surfaces are needed for ClearType, but the rectangular surface paints into the rounded panel’s corners. The current code clips the host window to a rounded region with `SetWindowRgn`, which clips drawing outside that shape. [host.rs:3001](/C:/Users/mshab/Projects/nex/apps/core/src/overlay/host.rs:3001) · [Microsoft’s window-region docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowrgn)

The latest issue comment also reports a brief frame on the first show, with later shows corrected. The code reapplies DWM chrome before revealing the window, then uncloaks it and syncs the rounded region before showing it. That points to a stale first DWM composition, but there’s no runtime trace confirming why it appears for that first frame. The current local commit, `a363607`, sets the opaque border to `DWMWA_COLOR_NONE` and adds the rounded clipping; the first-show behavior remains unverified.

content.text:
## Exact cause

The artifact is the **opaque WebView2 child window’s rectangular background**. In black and white modes, the overlay disables the DWM backdrop, and the WebView starts with an opaque background. The HTML panel’s 8 px radius clips the page, but the separate `WRY_WEBVIEW` child HWND had no matching rounded region. `SetWindowRgn` applies to the specific HWND passed to it, so rounding only the host left the child surface square. [Microsoft’s `SetWindowRgn` documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowrgn) · [WebView2 background behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/overview-features-apis)

The uneven background on first show came from reveal timing and geometry: the host was uncloaked before its final shape was synchronized, while Wry can resize its child during `WM_SIZE`. Later shows exposed the same child surface with square corners. This diagnosis follows from the show and resize paths in the code; Windows also tracks child-window visibility and clipping separately. [Microsoft’s child-window clipping documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/gdi/child-window-update-region)

I fixed this in [host.rs](/C:/Users/mshab/Projects/nex/apps/core/src/overlay/host.rs:3038): the host and WebView child now receive matching regions based on the client bounds; the maximum WebView viewport and regions are synchronized before reveal and after resize. Glass mode clears those regions.

**Commit:** `102274e fix(overlay): clip opaque WebView corners`  
**Verification:** `cargo check --release --bin Nex --bin NexHelper` passed. I did not run a live visual check.
